builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
summary: The method replaces conventional closed-form KL formulas and PyTorch F.kl_div with stable decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients that avoid catastrophic cancellation when comparing nearby distributions. Cost is limited to integrating the released stablekl library and re-validating existing KL-dependent code; there is no additional memory, latency, or infrastructure requirement. What can fail is incomplete coverage if the reader uses KL variants outside the 18 repaired families, and existing models trained under the biased gradients may shift behavior once losses are corrected, requiring re-tuning of hyperparameters that were implicitly calibrated to the old errors.
rationale: The fix is a drop-in replacement for standard KL formulas that requires no extra hardware or compute, and the paper demonstrates that current implementations silently corrupt losses, gradients, and downstream decisions even in single-GPU workflows.

claims.statement: The method replaces conventional closed-form KL formulas and PyTorch F.kl_div with stable decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients that avoid catastrophic cancellation when comparing nearby distributions. Cost is limited to integrating the released stablekl library and re-validating existing KL-dependent code; there is no additional memory, latency, or infrastructure requirement. What can fail is incomplete coverage if the reader uses KL variants outside the 18 repaired families, and existing models trained under the biased gradients may shift behavior once losses are corrected, requiring re-tuning of hyperparameters that were implicitly calibrated to the old errors.

Stable formulas and compensated arithmetic remove over 97% of significant KL errors in the working format; strict repairs eliminate significant errors on 7.2 million scored samples and correctly round all 567 million F.kl_div components, eliminating negative divergences and up to 97% top-1 disagreement in identical-start distillation.
